text: Large language models, or LLMs, are advanced computer programs trained on massive amounts of text from the internet, books, and articles. By analyzing patterns in this data, they learn to predict the next word in a sentence, which lets them generate coherent and detailed responses. To get a useful answer, users often practice prompt engineering—that is, crafting clear and specific questions or instructions. LLMs are incredibly capable: they can write essays, summarize documents, and even help with coding. However, they have limits. They sometimes invent facts, repeat biases from their training data, and lack real-world understanding. So, while they are powerful tools, they work best when you check their output and use them with care.
